biography.plain_text: Ronald L. Motley was an American trial lawyer and co-founder of Motley Rice, the South Carolina law firm. He built his fortune through large-scale litigation for people harmed by asbestos and tobacco. His work extended to representing September 11 victims' families, and he became known for forceful courtroom advocacy and preparation.

long_biography.plain_text:
For trial lawyer Ron Motley, some asbestos clients were familiar faces from childhood. He grew up helping at his father's petrol station near the Charleston naval base, pumping fuel, changing tyres and keeping the books. Years later, he represented some of the workers he had first met there.

Success in those cases supplied money for a much larger legal gamble. Motley and his partners reinvested their asbestos fees in tobacco litigation, paying the costs of cases whose outcome was far from certain. He concentrated on trial work while colleagues negotiated, combining witness testimony and internal company documents to challenge an industry with far greater resources.
